title: AI Agencies Just Got Simple Enough for Anyone to Start
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Flo describes Lindy as their company and repeatedly promotes its product; business use cases and performance figures are mostly anecdotal or promotional.

stated_problem.quote: you still have to learn the tool and ain't nobody got time for that
stated_problem.speaker: Flo

idea.name: Lindy AI agent platform
idea.one_liner: A platform for building and managing AI agents for business and personal workflows; revenue model is not stated.
idea.customer: Businesses and individual users who want to automate tasks.
idea.offer: A prompt-based AI agent builder with team collaboration and computer use.

key_quotes.quote: Lindy, which is an AI automation platform, came out with an update that enables anyone to create AI agents with one prompt.
So like now you can create an agent from just a prompt.
as long as this is a tool that is accessible from a web browser that is something that your agent is going to be able to use

ideas.delivery: Users create and run agents on Lindy; agents can use integrations or a virtual computer to perform browser-based tasks.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to personal data processed by agents. PECR applies to electronic marketing. Consumer-facing subscriptions may engage DMCC Act subscription requirements.

stated_problem.quote: massive opportunity to be the expert in the room for these business owners that know they need to be using AI but have no idea where to start.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: AI automation agency
idea.one_liner: An agency helps small and medium-sized businesses automate processes with AI agents and charges setup fees, retainers, or both.
idea.customer: Small and medium-sized businesses that need help identifying, building, and monitoring AI automations.
idea.offer: Consulting and implementation of agents for business workflows, potentially in a specialist vertical.
idea.revenue_model: Proposed setup fee and/or monthly retainer; examples are $500–$5,000 monthly or $300–$5,000 upfront plus $2–$700 monthly.

key_quotes.quote: starting an AI automation agency where you insert yourself into small to medium-sized businesses
use very cheap very easy to use tools to automate certain processes that these businesses use
each of them is an expert in their own vertical and each of them has their own existing network.

claims.claim: The host proposes charging $500–$5,000 per month.
claims.quote: you charge between $500 and $5,000 a month

claims.claim: The host proposes a $300–$5,000 one-time fee plus $2–$700 per month ongoing.
claims.quote: you charge $300 to $5,000 one time and $2 to $700 a month ongoing.

claims.claim: A hypothetical roofing automation pitch claims it could save a company $30,000 per month.
claims.quote: I can automate any of your processes and save you $30,000 a month

claims.claim: The host describes potential small-business clients as having $100,000–$10 million in revenue.
claims.quote: a plumbing business or a small business you know 100,000 to 10 million in revenue automate some of their processes

acquisition_channels.details: The guest says agencies have their own existing networks; no specific method is given.

ideas.delivery: The agency learns a client's workflows, builds and monitors agents, and provides ongoing consulting and support.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to client, staff, and customer data processed by agents. PECR applies to marketing; cold email to corporate subscribers needs sender identification and an opt-out, and sole traders are treated as individual subscribers. DMCC Act subscription requirements may apply to consumer subscriptions.

idea.name: AI SDR service
idea.one_liner: An AI sales development service finds prospects, researches and contacts them by email, qualifies replies, and books sales conversations; pricing is not stated.
idea.customer: Companies that want sales prospects and booked calls.
idea.offer: Automated lead research, personalized email outreach, objection handling, and qualification.

key_quotes.quote: fully autonomously not only like finds leads online and reaches them qualifies them
It handles objections. It it learns from the objections.
Like that's all the rage right now.

claims.claim: The guest says a dozen Silicon Valley companies focused on AI SDRs are raising tens of millions.
claims.quote: there are a dozen Silicon Valley companies right now raising tens of millions that are basically just that agent AISDR.

acquisition_channels.details: The agent finds leads, researches them, sends personalized emails, and handles follow-up conversations for clients.

ideas.delivery: The service runs agents that research prospects, email them, qualify responses, handle objections, and progress interested prospects toward calls.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to prospect data. PECR permits cold email to corporate subscribers with an opt-out; individual subscribers, including sole traders, generally require consent for unsolicited marketing email.

idea.name: AI-built qualified lead service for Salesforce reps
idea.one_liner: An operator uses an AI agent to find and engage prospects, then sells a qualified, interested lead and its conversation to a Salesforce sales representative.
idea.customer: Salesforce representatives who want qualified prospective customers.
idea.offer: A warm lead with the prospect's identity, contact details, and prior conversation.
idea.revenue_model: Payment per lead; amount is negotiated and not stated.

key_quotes.quote: I go find a bunch of potential clients, I go create an AI sales development a agent in Lindy
Hey, I have a really hot lead for you.
Here's the whole conversation. Here's his name, phone, email.

claims.claim: The host estimates the lead could be worth 4,000 MR to the company; the unit is spoken as “MR” in the transcript.
claims.quote: I'm guessing it's going to be worth 4,000 MR to your company

claims.claim: The host estimates that a generic cold pitch has about a half-percent reply chance.
claims.quote: Your chance of getting a reply to that is like half a percent.

claims.claim: The host rhetorically claims a lead supplied with its conversation would have a 100% reply chance.
claims.quote: What's your chance of getting a reply to that conversation? 100%.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to prospect contact data. PECR permits cold email to corporate subscribers with an opt-out; sole traders and individual subscribers need consent for unsolicited marketing email.

idea.name: AI-assisted recruiting firm
idea.one_liner: A recruiting firm uses agents to identify candidates matching open roles, contacts them, and earns a placement fee when a hire is made.
idea.customer: Companies hiring for roles such as software engineering.
idea.offer: Candidate sourcing, outreach, interview booking, and placement tracking.
idea.revenue_model: Contingency placement fee; the guest describes 20% of first-year salary as an example used by some recruiting companies.

key_quotes.quote: they look at the list of job descriptions that the company has on its career page.
it goes on LinkedIn and finds people that satisfy these requirements
you don't pay me anything unless I actually get you a hire through the door.

claims.claim: The recruiting firm says it found three candidates matching a client's requirements.
claims.quote: Three leads that we found that satisfy your requirements.

claims.claim: The recruiting firm claims it has a thousand more similar leads.
claims.quote: We've got a thousand more like those.

claims.claim: The guest says some recruiting companies charge 20% of the first salary on a contingency basis.
claims.quote: you only pay us 20% of the first salary, which is a lot of money.

claims.claim: The guest characterizes that example fee as $30,000 or more.
claims.quote: which is a lot of money. It's like $30,000 plus.

claims.claim: The proposed agent checks candidates' LinkedIn profiles monthly to see whether they joined a client.
claims.quote: another AI agent that checks every month the LinkedIn profiles

acquisition_channels.details: The firm emails hiring companies with sample candidates and offers to send more or begin outreach.

ideas.delivery: Agents collect job requirements, search LinkedIn for matching candidates, contact them, support interview booking, and track placements; people may still need to handle client and candidate relationships.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Employment Agencies Act 1973 and Conduct of Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003 may apply. UK GDPR governs candidate data; PECR rules depend on whether outreach is marketing and the subscriber type.

idea.name: Free Linktree competitor for influencers
idea.one_liner: A free link-in-bio product gives influencers a page to promote products, newsletters, or other links; monetization is not stated.
idea.customer: Influencers and creators, with the example targeting US-based Instagram influencers.
idea.offer: A free alternative to Linktree that can host creator links and promotions.

key_quotes.quote: find me a US-based influencer with at least 50,000 subscribers
build me a linkree competitor with your vibe coding tool.
Use mine. You have 50,000 subscribers.

claims.claim: The proposed prospect list targets influencers with at least 50,000 subscribers.
claims.quote: find me a US-based influencer with at least 50,000 subscribers

claims.claim: The pitch compares the free competitor with a Linktree price of $20 per month.
claims.quote: Don't pay Linkree 20 bucks a month.

acquisition_channels.details: The example finds influencers on Instagram and sends an unsolicited promotional message.

ideas.delivery: Build a free link-in-bio product with a vibe-coding tool and invite influencers to use it.

uk_legal_risk.reason: The acquisition example relies on unsolicited promotional social messages to individual influencers. The cited target is US-based, but the same approach to UK individuals or sole traders would breach PECR rules for marketing DMs.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to influencer contact data. PECR applies to promotional DMs sent to UK individuals; lawful basis, transparency, and opt-out requirements also apply to personal data processing.

idea.name: Comment and DM management service for publishers
idea.one_liner: A service uses agents to moderate comments and respond to audience DMs for content publishers, charging a monthly fee.
idea.customer: Creators, publishers, and brands that receive high volumes of comments or DMs.
idea.offer: Sentiment-based comment moderation, spam and abuse removal, and tailored replies or thank-yous in DMs.
idea.revenue_model: Monthly service fee; amount is not stated.

key_quotes.quote: you can offer this as a service for people that don't want to read all these toxic comments
people that want to kindly respond to people in their DMs.
this is a service you could offer for a monthly fee just using Lindy on the back end.

claims.claim: The example agent is shown handling 3,300 LinkedIn comments.
claims.quote: 3300 comments responding agent. So, when we had that, we're like, "Oh, this is a pain. We need to answer like 3,300 people."

claims.claim: The host estimates the automation would save 55 hours if it replaced manual replies at the stated pace.
claims.quote: that is 55 hours right here saved just not having to go and respond to those manually.

claims.claim: The host uses one minute per comment as a lower-bound estimate in the time-saving calculation.
claims.quote: even if it only takes one minute to do per comments

claims.claim: The host says he pays about $350 per month for ManyChat for a similar function.
claims.quote: I'm I'm paying like $350 a month for ManyHat, which just does this.

claims.claim: The host says he receives thousands of comments per day on Instagram and Facebook.
claims.quote: I get thousands of comments per day on Instagram and Facebook

ideas.delivery: Agents monitor publishers' comments and DMs, remove spam or bad-faith comments, and send tailored responses; escalations may need human review.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to audience comments and DM data. PECR applies if the service sends unsolicited direct marketing DMs to UK individuals; consent and platform rules should be considered.

idea.name: Cold email agency
idea.one_liner: An agency finds companies that want outbound email and uses agents to prospect, verify contacts, send campaigns, handle replies, close clients, and collect payment.
idea.customer: Companies seeking cold email prospecting and sales conversations.
idea.offer: End-to-end outbound email campaign setup and execution.

key_quotes.quote: my customers are companies that want to send cold emails
I could use cold emails to find my customers, I could use Lindy to do that.
craft, scrape, verify, send, reply to, reply to again, reply to again, close.

acquisition_channels.details: The agency uses cold emails to find its own customers and runs cold email campaigns for clients.

ideas.delivery: Agents research and verify contact data, compose and send emails, manage replies and follow-ups, support closing, and collect payments through Stripe.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to prospect data. Under PECR, cold email is permitted to corporate subscribers with an opt-out, but unsolicited marketing email to individual subscribers, including sole traders, generally requires consent.
